summary: This is the Thermostat class with eco mode, plus a new printStatusToDisplay method that writes the current status to the console. It shows how a method that prints instead of returning a value is harder to test later.

lines.text: The current temperature is stored as final, so it is set once when the thermostat is created and never changes afterwards.
A true/false flag recording whether the thermostat is running in energy-saving mode.
The constructor takes both settings at once, so every Thermostat object exists in a fully configured state.
The conditional operator picks 65 in eco mode and 68 otherwise, letting the house get cooler before the heat comes on when saving energy.
Likewise, eco mode tolerates a warmer room before cooling starts.
Below the heating threshold the thermostat calls for heat, so this check comes first.
If neither threshold was crossed, the temperature is comfortable and nothing needs to run.

A void method returns nothing, so the only way to observe its work is by watching the console ise
 needs to capture that output to test it.
The message reuses getStatus rather than repeating the threshold logic, keeping the decision rules in a single place.
